questions.question: How many Lok Sabha constituencies are there in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**543**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lok Sabha**, also known as the** House of the People**, is the **lower house** of India's bicameral Parliament.
 
• Its **members are chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage to represent their respective constituencies**, and they serve terms of **five years** or until the body is dissolved by the President on the recommendation of the council of ministers.
 
• The Lok Sabha is composed of representatives of people chosen by direct election on the basis of Universal Adult Suffrage.
 
• The Constitution of India allows for a maximum of 550 members in the House, with 530 members representing the States and 20 representing the Union Territories.
 
• At present, the Lok Sabha has 543 seats filled by elected representatives. The term of the Lok Sabha, unless dissolved, is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting.
 
• However, while a proclamation of emergency is in operation, this period may be extended by Parliament by law for a period not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case, beyond a period of six months after the proclamation has ceased to operate.
 
• There are now **543 Lok Sabha constituencies in In****dia**, with the **most constituencies** being in **Uttar Pradesh (80)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha** together make up the **Parliament of India**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha** are both essential parts of India's parliament. The Lok sabha has** 543 members**, whereas the Rajya sabha has **250 members** .
 
• The majority of **state-related decisions **are made based on votes cast by Rajya sabha members, but **no decision may be made for the state without the consent of the Lok Sabha **members.
 
• Both the** Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha** are chosen by a simple **majority of the members present and voting** to serve as the House's presiding authorities. The Constitution merely stipulates that the **Speaker must be a member of the House**; no other requirements are set forth for election as Speaker.

questions.question: In 1887, the Royal Society, London gave the Davy Medal for the ‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ to _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Alexander Newland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1887, the Royal Society, London** gave the **Davy Medal **for the **‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ **to **John Alexander Newland**.
 
• British chemist, **John Alexander Reina Newlands** specialised in **elemental periodicity**.
 
• **John Newlands **was the first to create a **table of chemical elements grouped according to their respective atomic weight**.
 
• He made his idea of the **periodicity of the chemical elements**, which he had arranged in order of atomic weight, public in** 1864**.
 
• In order to make a **connection with musical octaves**, Newlands named this phenomenon,** The Law of Octaves** after noticing **commonalities between elements whose atomic weights varied by seven**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first person to arrange chemical elements according to their atomic weights was** AEB de Chancourtois**, who also created an **early version of the periodic table known as the "telluric helix" because tellurium was in the centre**.
 
• Russian chemist and inventor **Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev** is best known for conceiving th**e Periodic Law and developing a preliminary version of the periodic table of elements**.
 
• A pioneer in creating the** first iterations of the periodic table of chemical elements** was the German chemist **Julius Lothar Meyer**.

questions.question: In November 2022, Technology Transfer Scheme is implemented by which of these states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Technology Transfer Scheme** was implemented by the state of **Kerala **in **November 2022**.
 
• The **government will reimburse companies up to 10 lakh **under the Technology Transfer Scheme**,** run by **Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM)**, **for technologies they acquire from government research institutions or source themselves and use to create potentially marketable items**.
 
• With the aid of this programme, **startups of Kerala** will have easier access to the knowledge needed to **transform their concepts into goods that can be sold**.
 
• Startups that are **registered as Limited Liability Partnerships (LLP) or Private Limited companies in Kerala** and have an **active registration with the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM) **are eligible for the technology transfer scheme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transfer of Technology (ToT) or technology transfer** is the** transfer of data **such as designs, inventions, materials, software, trade secrets, and technical know-how **from one organisation to another or from one use to another**.
 
• The **rules, practises, and principles of any organisation taking part in the technology transfer process serve as guidelines**.
 
• In order to share skills, knowledge, technologies, production techniques, and other things, universities, businesses, and governments can engage in **formal or informal technology transfer**. 
 
• This method of knowledge sharing **ensures that scientific and technological advancements are accessible to more user**s, who can then contribute to their growth or utilisation.
 
• Technology transfer can t**ake place vertically by shifting technologies or horizontally by moving technologies **between various regions.

questions.question: Who among the following performed a ritual called ‘hiranya-garbha’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dantidurga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rashtrakuta leader, Dantidurga** deposed the **Chalukyas **after deciding that he wanted to be more than a Samanta.
 
• After engaging in a ceremony known as the** 'hiranya-garbha'**, he** proclaimed himself as the king of the Deccan region of the Chalukyas and formed the Rashtrakuta Empire**.
 
• According to** Vedic philosophy**, the **origin of the universe or the manifested cosmos is known as hiranya-garbha**, which means **"golden womb" or "universal womb"**.
 
• With the assistance of Brahmanas, **Dantidurga completed the hiranya-garbha ceremony**, signifying his **rebirth** as a Kshatriya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Around **780 CE**, Rashtrakuta ruler named, **Dhruva Dharavarsha** seized power over the realm.
 
• **Dhruva Dharavarsha** made the kingdom so large that it included the entire area between the Kaveri River and Central India.
 
• **Dantidurga's uncle, Krishna I** overthrew **Kirtivarman II, the last Badami Chalukya king, in 757 CE **to assume control of the expanding **Rashtrakuta Empire.**

questions.question: Which of the following Acts of the British Parliament stated that a member of the British Cabinet was appointed Secretary of State for India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act of 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act of 1858** was the **Act of the British Parliament** which stated that a** member of the British Cabinet was appointed Secretary of State for India**.
 
• The** Government of India Act 1858** was enacted by the British Parliament on** 2 August 1858**.
 
• With the passage of the Government of India Act 1858, the E**ast India Company's territories and government were turned over to the British Crown**.
 
• Following the **end of the company's administration over British colonies in India**, control was transferred directly to the British government.
 
• **Lord Stanley** was appointed as the **first Secretary of State for India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Indian Councils Act 1861** was an Act of the British Parliament that **changed the executive council of India into a cabinet that utilised the portfolio system**.
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was an Act of the British Parliament d**esigned to restructure the East India Company's administration of its rule in India**.
 
• The British Parliament enacted the **Charter Act, 1853 to extend the charter of the East India Company**.

questions.question: Against whom was the Battle of Plassey (1757) fought by the English Company led by Robert Clive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siraj Ud Daulah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** East India Company** force led by** Robert Clive** and** Siraj-Ud-Daulah**, the **Nawab of Bengal**, engaged in a battle on** June 23, 1757, at Plassey**, in response to the East India Company's** misuse of trade privileges**, which infuriated the Nawab.
 
• **Mir Jafar, the chief commander** of Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah,** defected**, which allowed for the victory of East India Company.
 
• With Clive's triumph, the British rose to become India's dominant economic and military force after **capturing Calcutta**.
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** took place at a site called** Palashi (or Plassey),** on the banks of the Hooghly River, about 150 kilometres north of Calcutta and south of Murshidabad, which was then the capital of Bengal Subah.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The title of the kings who ruled the state of** Awadh in north India** during the **18th and 19th centuries **was** "Nawab of Awadh"** or **"Nawab of Oudh"**.
 
• **First Nawab of Bengal, Murshid Quli Khan** reigned from **1717 to 1727 **and was also known as **Zamin Ali Quli**. He was born as hindu and was originally called, **Surya Narayan Mishra**.

questions.question: In July 2022, the Supreme Court accepted the report of the Banthia Commission. In its report, the commission recommended that OBCs should be given up to _______ reservation in local bodies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**27 percent**__**.**

__
 
• The report produced by Jayantkumar Banthia Commission, recommended that OBCs should be given up to 27 percent reservation in local bodies. 
 
• This report is accepted by court, and it confirmed that OBCs will get 27 percent political reservation in local self-government elections in the state.
 
• In case of direct recruitment to Group C and D posts which normally attract candidates from a locality or a region, the percentage of reservation forSCs /STs is generally fixed in proportion to the population of SCs and STs.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​ This report made a way for candidates who belong to Other Backward Classes in Local Bodies’ Elections in Maharashtra.
 
• Commission has recommended to provide 27& reservation in local bodies. 
 
• This recommendation has been accepted by the supreme court. 
 
• As per report, reservation should be provided to OBCs in proportion to their population in each local body. 
 
• However, this reservation should not affect the statutory reservation for scheduled castes and scheduled tribes. It is subject to reservation limit of 50%.

questions.question: The mode of transport to reach the most remote and distant areas which are most inaccessible is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Airways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the early twentieth century, it is the fastest way of transport developed and **most expensive due to the high cost of fuels.**
 
• It is the only mode of transport to reach the most distant and remote areas especially where there are no railways and roads.
 
• For rescuing people and distributing medicine, water, clothes, and food, **helicopters** are extremely useful in most **inaccessible areas **and in times of **calamities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Railways**: railway is a kind of transport that needs railway tracks in the destination region, sometimes, the service is found unavailable or difficult to use.
 
• **Roadways**: A natural disaster can cause loss of life or damage property and typically leaves some economic damages. It firstly damages the road network that restricts transport by heavy vehicles.
 
• **Waterways**: Waterways also require a seaport to reach ,but it sometimes becomes unavailable for the services or located far away from the area.

questions.question: How many rights are mentioned under “Right to Equality”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __5__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to equality is one of the **five fundamental rights in the Indian constitution, **which are:

 
 
• This right of equality in **law, prohibition of discrimination on grounds of race, religion, gender, and caste or birthplace**.
 
• It also includes** equality of opportunity in matters of employment and abolition of untouchability and titles**.
 
• In a few words, it can be said that it is the right to live with equal opportunities.
 
• It implies treating all people in the same way and nobody can be treated privileged that may dishonor any individual or group.
 
• Article no 14 of our constitution, it guarantees that all people shall be equally protected by the laws of the country. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Article 14 **provides for equality in general. 
 
• **Article 21 **guarantees the right to life and liberty.
 
• Article 15 prohibits Page 14 14 discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• This concept is borrowed from British Constitution.

questions.question: Which low-calorie sweetener has the chemical formula C₁₄H₁₈N₂O₅ that is two hundred times sweeter than sugar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aspartame.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aspartame is **an artificial non-saccharide sweetener 200 times sweeter than sucrose** and is commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
 
• It is a **methyl ester of the aspartic acid/phenylalanine dipeptide**.
 
• **Chemical formula:** C₁₄ H₁₈ N₂ O₅ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saccharin**

 
 
• Saccharin often used in the form of sodium saccharin, is **an artificial sweetener with effectively no nutritional value.**
 
• It is about **550 times as sweet as sucrose** but has a bitter or metallic aftertaste, especially at high concentrations.
 
• Saccharin is used to sweeten products such as drinks, candies, cookies, especially for masking the bitter taste of some medicines.
 
 
 
• **Sucralose**
 
 
• It is a general-purpose sweetener that can be found in a variety of foods including baked goods, beverages, chewing gum, gelatins, and frozen dairy desserts.
 
• It is heat stable, meaning that it stays sweet even when used at high temperatures during baking, making it suitable as a sugar substitute in baked goods.
 
 
 
• **Neotame**
 
 
• The safety studies found that long-term neotame consumption is associated with low body weight and low body weight gain, although this has long been considered the result of low food consumption

questions.question: Techniques of making silk were first invented in China around _____ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**7000**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of silk production is known as **sericulture.**
 
• It was **discovered by the Chinese 7000 **years ago.
 
• According to legend, the** princess Xi Lingshi discovered** that a cocoon could be unraveled to produce a thread when one dropped into her tea while sat under a mulberry tree.
 
• The secret of silk production is the tiny creature known as the silk worm, the most common being the **Bombyx Mori**.
 
• A flightless, domesticated moth, it lays 500 eggs in 5 days and then dies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silk Route:**

 
 
• **​**The Silk Route was a network of **Eurasian trade routes active from the second century BCE until the mid-15th century.**
 
• Spanning over 6,400 kilometers.,
 
• It played a **central role in facilitating economic, cultural, political, and religious interactions** between the East and West.
 
• The name "Silk Road", first coined in the late 19th century, has fallen into disuse among some modern historians in favor of Silk Routes,
 
• It describes the intricate web of land and sea routes** connecting East and Southeast Asia**, **the Indian subcontinent, Central Asia, the Middle East, East Africa and Europe.**

questions.question: The first edition of the Common wealth Youth Games was organised in which of the following years?

__
 
• The Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) is an international **multi-sport event **organized by **the Commonwealth Games Federation. **
 
• The games were held in the years, mid-way between when **the Commonwealth Games** are held, and 2008.
 
• They continued to be held every four years, but in the year after the Commonwealth Games are held, from 2011 to 2015.
 
• Since 2017, they've been held in the year before the Commonwealth Games are held.
 
• The **first edition** was held in Edinburgh, Scotland from 10–14 August 2000.
 
• The age limitation of the athletes is **from 14 to 18**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Commonwealth Youth Games 2023**

 
 
• The 2023 Commonwealth Youth Games will be held in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. The games were originally scheduled to be held in 2021, but were postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The games will now be held from 4 to 11 August 2023.
 
• The Commonwealth Youth Games are a multi-sport event for athletes aged 14 to 18. The games are held every four years and are organized by the Commonwealth Games Federation. The 2023 Commonwealth Youth Games will be the seventh edition of the games.
 
• The games will feature 10 sports: athletics, badminton, boxing, cycling, gymnastics, judo, netball, rugby sevens, swimming, and tennis. There will also be a cultural program that will feature music, dance, and art from the Commonwealth.

questions.question: The ceremony that marks the end of Republic Day celebrations is ________.

options.text: the fly-past by the Indian Air Force fighter aircraft
the ‘At Home’ ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhawan
the homage ceremony at National War Memorial

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the beating retreat ceremony**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beating Retreat Ceremony** is a military ceremony dating back to 17th-century England.
 
• The Beating Retreat Ceremony was originally known as **‘Watch Setting’**.
 
• This Ceremony was first used to recall nearby** patrolling units to their castle.**
 
• It was initiated at sunset by the firing of a single round from the evening gun.
 
• The Beating Retreat Ceremonies usually consist of firing a canon, marching a band, and other decorative presentations.
 
• Currently, most of the armed forces in the ‘Commonwealth’ perform some ceremonial form of retreat. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to **Wing Commander Indranil Nandi**, the Republic Day fly-past will feature 45 Indian Air Force (IAF) aircraft, one Indian Navy aircraft, and four Indian Army helicopters.
 
• **At Home’ ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhawan**, It is an opportunity for people from various walks to meet the PM (Prime Minister) and the President and to interact with each other.
 
• PM Modi pays tribute to fallen soldiers at **National War Memorial** on Republic Day.

questions.question: Polar easterlies are which kind of winds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Permanent winds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Polar easterlies are dry, cold prevailing winds that blow from the east.
 
• They emanate from the polar highs, areas of high pressure around the North and South Poles.
 
• Polar easterlies flow to low-pressure areas in sub-polar regions.
 
• Westerlies are prevailing winds that blow from the west at mid-latitudes.
 
• These winds are also called trades winds because winds blow from subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low-pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information __**

 
• **Seasonal winds**

 
 
• The winds which change their direction in different seasons.
 
• For example, the monsoons in India are seasonal winds. 
 
 
 
• **Sea ****storm**
 
 
• **The Sun's heat causes **ocean surface waters to evaporate. 
 
• The warm, moist air rises, cools, and condenses to form clouds.
 
• If the air is warm enough, large thunderstorms can form. 
 
 
 
• **Local winds**
 
 
• **This wind ****flow are** caused by the uneven heat of the Earth's surface within a small area.
 
• Local winds form only when strong winds are weak.

questions.question: Identify the longest part of the bacterial flagellum.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Filament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The motile bacterias** have thin filamentous extensions from their cell wall called **flagella**. 
 
• Bacteria show a range in** the number and arrangement of flagella.**
 
• The bacterial flagellum is made up of three parts:
 
 
• Filament 
 
• Hook
 
• Basal body
 
 
 
• **The filament is the longest portion **and extends from the cell surface to the outside.
 
• This filament consists of Protein which is known as a bacteria cytoskeleton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Flagellum

 
 
• It is primarily a motility organelle that enables movement and chemotaxis.
 
• Bacteria can have one flagellum or several, and they can be either polar (one or several flagella at one spot) or peritrichous (several flagella all over the bacterium).
 
 
 
• Gram-negative bacteria
 
 
• The example of the bacteria Escherichia coli and Salmonella swim by rotating helical filamentous organelles called the flagellum.
 
• The flagellum rotates at a speed of 200–300 Hz driven by a reversible rotary motor embedded in the cell membrane at the base of the filament.

__
 
• **Borgeet**__, a musical composition, is used in __**Sattriya**__.
 
• It is composed for **Madhavdeb** and **Sankardev** based on classical raga.
 
• The instruments include Khol (asymmetrical drum), Cymbals, manjira, flute, violin, harmonium, etc.​
 
• Some eminent personality who contributed importance are Late Moniram Dutta, Muktiyar Barban etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• ​Manipuri dance

 
 
• It is counted among major classical dance forms of India, especially noted for themes based on Vaishnavism and spectacular execution of 'Ras Lila', dance dramas based on love between Radha and Krishna. 
 
 
 
• Kathak dance
 
 
• It is originated from Uttar Pradesh (U.P) in North India.
 
• This one is derived from the word Katha meaning story, and during the whole dance, the dancers narrate stories through their eyes and expressions.
 
 
 
• Bharatanatyam dance
 
 
• In this dance for style is noted for its fixed upper torso, bent legs and knees flexed (Araimandi) combined with footwork, and a vocabulary of sign language based on gestures of hands, eyes, and face muscles.

questions.question: Which of the following cells line the spongocoels and canals in members of the phylum Porifera?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Collar cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The body of** sponges (poriferans) **has several minute pores called **ostia** through which the water enters into the central cavity, spongocoel.
 
• The flagellated cells called** choanocytes (collar cells)** line the spongocoel.
 
• These cells generate **a flow of water and the water current helps in food gathering, respiratory exchange and removal of waste.**
 
• The water finally goes out of the body through a large pore called **osculum**. (Plural: oscula).
 
• The body wall of the sponge is composed of two layers: **outer pinacoderm and inner choanoderm**. In between these two layers, mesenchyme is present with various **mesenchymal cells.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Somatic cells make up the connective tissue, skin, blood, bones and internal organs.
 
• White blood cells are made in the bone marrow. They are stored in your blood and lymph tissues.
 
• These sex cells are also called reproductive cells or gametes. Sperm cells are produced in men's testicles and egg cells are produced in women's ovaries

questions.question: If marginal propensity to consume is denoted by c, then government expenditure multiplier can be expressed as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1/1-c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The magnitude of the multiplier is directly related to the marginal propensity to consume (MPC), which is defined as **the proportion of an increase in income that gets spent on consumption.**
 
• MPC stands for **Marginal Propensity to Consume**.
 
• It is defined as the proportion of an aggregate raise in income that is spent by a consumer on goods and services instead of saving it. 
 
• Expenditure multiplier=** 1over Marginal\: propensity\: to\: save**
 
• We also know Marginal Propensity to save =**1- Marginal propensity to consume = 1 - c**
 
 
• **i.e. **Saving = Income - consume.
 
• here Income taken as 1 to ease the understand.
 
 
 
• Therefore if we can express the **expenditure multiplier = 1over 1-c**
